questions.stem: The 'BRICS' grouping originally comprised five countries. The 'S' stands for:

options.option_text: Singapore
South Africa
Saudi Arabia
Sri Lanka

questions.explanation: BRIC (2006) — Brazil, Russia, India, China — became BRICS in 2010 with the addition of South Africa. The group is expanding — as of 1 January 2024, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the UAE joined; Saudi Arabia has been formally invited, Argentina declined. The New Development Bank (NDB) is headquartered in Shanghai.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a member of OPEC (Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries)?

options.option_text: Saudi Arabia
India
Iran
Venezuela

questions.explanation: OPEC — 13 founding / continuing members (as of 2024) — Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Venezuela (founding 5, 1960) + Algeria, Libya, Nigeria, UAE, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Congo, and others. India is a net oil importer, not a producer-exporter of any scale — and not an OPEC member. OPEC+ (since 2016) is a broader grouping that includes Russia, Kazakhstan, Mexico and others.

questions.stem: The G20 presidency for 2023 was held by India. Which member's flag was the backdrop of the New Delhi summit's logo design?

options.option_text: The lotus
The peacock
The tiger
The Ashoka chakra only

questions.explanation: The 2023 G20 India presidency logo incorporated the lotus — the national flower. Theme — 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' / 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'. At the New Delhi summit (September 2023), the African Union was admitted as the 21st permanent member. India passed the presidency to Brazil for 2024. The G20 includes the G7, BRICS and most major economies.

questions.stem: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) was founded in which year in response to the Cold War?
questions.explanation: NATO was established on 4 April 1949 by the North Atlantic Treaty (Washington Treaty). Originally 12 members; now 32 (Finland joined 2023, Sweden 2024). HQed in Brussels. Core principle — Article 5, collective defence (an attack on one is an attack on all), invoked only once (after 9/11, 2001). Warsaw Pact (the Soviet-led counter) was founded in 1955 and dissolved in 1991.

questions.stem: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) comprises how many member states?

options.option_text: Seven
Ten
Twelve
Fourteen

questions.explanation: ASEAN — 10 members: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam. Founded 1967 (Bangkok Declaration) by 5 founding members. Secretariat in Jakarta. Timor-Leste has been an observer since 2022 (with full admission anticipated). India is a dialogue partner + 'Act East Policy' and participates in ASEAN-led forums like the East Asia Summit.

questions.stem: India is a founding member of which regional economic grouping formed in 1985?

options.option_text: ASEAN
SAARC
APEC
NAFTA

questions.explanation: SAARC — 8 member states (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Maldives + Afghanistan since 2007). Founded in Dhaka, 8 December 1985; secretariat in Kathmandu. Despite initial hopes, SAARC has been hobbled by India-Pakistan tensions — no summit has been held since Kathmandu 2014. India's alternative focus has increasingly been on BIMSTEC (India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand) — excluding Pakistan.

questions.stem: The European Union (EU) currently has how many member states?
questions.explanation: EU — 27 members. The UK formally left the EU on 31 January 2020 (Brexit), reducing the membership from 28 to 27. Croatia was the latest to join (2013). HQ — Brussels. Common currency — the Euro (€), shared by 20 of the 27 members (the 'Eurozone'). Schengen area (free movement) is a related but distinct overlapping grouping.

questions.stem: The 'Quad' (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) is a strategic grouping comprising which four nations?

options.option_text: United States, Japan, South Korea, and India
United States, Japan, Australia, and India
United States, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines
United States, United Kingdom, Australia, and India

questions.explanation: The Quad (revived 2017) consists of USA, Japan, Australia, and India, united around a free and open Indo-Pacific vision. The UK is NOT a Quad member — it belongs to the separate AUKUS pact (USA, UK, Australia). South Korea and the Philippines engage informally but are not formal Quad members. Option A substitutes South Korea, a common confusion since Seoul is a close US ally.

questions.stem: The OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) has its permanent headquarters in which city?

options.option_text: Geneva, Switzerland — host of many UN specialised bodies
Brussels, Belgium — home to EU institutions and NATO HQ
Paris, France — where the founding OECD Convention was signed
Vienna, Austria — home to OPEC and IAEA headquarters

questions.explanation: The OECD Convention was signed in Paris on 14 December 1960 and the Secretariat is at Château de la Muette, Paris. Vienna hosts OPEC and IAEA, Geneva hosts WHO and WTO, and Brussels hosts EU and NATO — all genuine international-organisation hubs that make this a meaningful recall test, not trivial elimination.

questions.stem: India is a 'Dialogue Partner' but NOT a full member of which of the following groupings?

options.option_text: BIMSTEC — the Bay of Bengal grouping of seven riparian nations
SCO — the Eurasian security and economic cooperation bloc
ASEAN — the ten-nation Southeast Asian political-economic bloc
IORA — the Indian Ocean regional association of 23 member states

questions.explanation: ASEAN restricts full membership to Southeast Asian nations; India has been a Dialogue Partner since 1992 and a Summit-level Partner since 2002 but is NOT a member. India is a founding member of both BIMSTEC (1997) and IORA (1997), and became a full SCO member in June 2017. Confusion arises because India's ASEAN Summit-level involvement visually resembles membership.

questions.stem: In WTO trade rounds, the 'Cairns Group' is a coalition of 19 agricultural exporting nations that lobbies primarily for which objective?

options.option_text: Establishing mandatory minimum farm-support payments for developing nations
Liberalising global agricultural trade and ending rich-country farm subsidies
Protecting domestic food security through higher agricultural import tariffs
Creating a global strategic grain reserve managed by the United Nations

questions.explanation: The Cairns Group (formed 1986, Cairns, Australia) is a free-trade-in-agriculture bloc pushing for elimination of export subsidies and domestic-support distortions — especially those of the EU and USA. A common wrong instinct is to assume it protects agriculture; it does the opposite. Notably, India is NOT a Cairns Group member because India's position defends food-security tariffs.

questions.stem: India withdrew from RCEP negotiations in November 2019. Which of the following best captures the primary stated reason for India's exit?

options.option_text: Services trade access demands were rejected by RCEP partner nations
Domestic industry feared import surge, especially of cheap goods from China
Patent norms would have restricted India's generic pharmaceutical exports
Digital economy and e-commerce interests were sidelined in the RCEP text

questions.explanation: The Indian government cited the risk of a surge in cheap imports — particularly Chinese manufactured goods — exploiting RCEP tariff cuts through third-country routes. India's trade deficit with China was already substantial, and the proposed price-trigger safeguard clauses were deemed inadequate. Services access (A) and pharma IP norms (C) were secondary negotiating concerns, not the decisive announced reason.

questions.stem: The Visegrad Group (V4) is a Central European cooperation framework of four EU member states. Which of the following is NOT a V4 member?

options.option_text: Romania — a Central European EU member state that joined the EU in 2007
Slovakia — a founding V4 member since the 1991 Visegrad Declaration
Hungary — Central European nation and founding V4 member since 1991
Poland — the largest V4 economy and a founding member since 1991

questions.explanation: The V4 comprises Poland, Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia — all signatories of the 1991 Visegrad Declaration. Romania, despite being a Central European EU state, was never admitted; it participates only in ad-hoc V4+ consultations. The most common error is substituting Romania for Slovakia, which is the least-recalled of the four genuine members.

questions.stem: The Lima Group, formed by the Lima Declaration of August 2017 and comprising 12 Latin American nations plus Canada, was convened primarily to address the political and humanitarian crisis in which country?

options.option_text: Cuba — amid sustained international criticism of its single-party system
Bolivia — following disputed 2019 elections and President Morales's exit
Venezuela — amid constitutional crisis, economic collapse, and mass exodus
Nicaragua — following Ortega's crackdown on civil society and opposition

questions.explanation: The Lima Group was created in August 2017 specifically to respond to Venezuela's constitutional violations under Maduro, hyperinflationary economic collapse, and mass emigration (over 7 million people). Bolivia's 2019 crisis post-dated the Group's formation, making Option B a strong chronological trap. Nicaragua and Cuba, while authoritarian contexts, were not the founding trigger. The Group formally wound down circa 2022–23.
